question: Roger authorized a one-time application of the data-rights migration to the dedicated synthetic acceptance project. Can this session perform it, and can it satisfy the authorization's own preconditions?

whatTheAuthorizationRequiredFirst.step2_recordFiveFacts: PARTIAL — three of five recorded below; two cannot be produced here
whatTheAuthorizationRequiredFirst.step3_confirmSixConditions: NOT POSSIBLE — every one of them is a statement about a project this session cannot reach

integratedCommits: 959b3bd10dfcc2845be894738424a1967dcc8781 — replay onto the current Captain head
caaab8447b1bc6640ea9580a9c8387064215343c — governance regenerated from the current tree
recorded.thisMigrationIsNext: 20260830120000_participant_data_rights.sql is the next identity in the forward-only timestamped chain and applies through it normally.
recorded.nonproductionProjectRefWhyNull: No project ref is configured in this session and none is recorded in the repository for a synthetic acceptance project. Inventing one, or reusing a ref found in an unrelated record, would be fabricating the single fact the authorization is keyed to.
recorded.dedicatedSyntheticAcceptanceProofWhyNull: Proof that a project is dedicated to synthetic acceptance is an observation about that project's contents. It cannot be asserted from here; it has to be read from the project.

whyItCannotRunHere.evidence: No SUPABASE_* environment variable is set in this session — no project ref, no service-role key, no database URL. docs/rcap/grade-a/captain/decision-waiting/nonproduction-readiness-audit.json already records SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF as absent, so this is a standing condition rather than a new one.

https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects and https://supabase.com both return http_code 000 (the CONNECT tunnel is refused before any request is sent), while https://registry.npmjs.org/ returns 200. That is the same allowlist policy the acquisition probe characterised on 2026-08-30: package registries permitted, everything else denied. A managed project cannot be reached from this environment even with a credential.
The Supabase CLI is not installed. psql is present, but it has nothing to connect to.

theSixConfirmationsAndWhyEachIsBlocked.noRealParticipantAccountsOrRecords: An observation about the project's tables. Requires reading the project.
theSixConfirmationsAndWhyEachIsBlocked.noProductionDatabaseOrEnvironmentConnect: An observation about the project's configuration. Requires reading the project.
theSixConfirmationsAndWhyEachIsBlocked.allTestIdentitiesAndRecordsSynthetic: An observation about rows that do not yet exist, in a project that cannot be reached.
theSixConfirmationsAndWhyEachIsBlocked.processorCallbacksUseSyntheticEndpointsO: Configurable here in principle, but meaningless to assert without the environment it would be configured in.
theSixConfirmationsAndWhyEachIsBlocked.migrationRunsThroughTheTimestampedChain: This one IS confirmable from the repository, and it holds: the file sits at the end of supabase/migrations/ and carries no phase-NN identity.
theSixConfirmationsAndWhyEachIsBlocked.obsoletePhase57NotApplied: Also confirmable, and it holds: no phase-57 file exists in this tree. The draft was never integrated and the rebuilt migration replaces it.

whatWouldUnblockIt: A session or operator environment that holds the synthetic acceptance project's ref and service-role credential, and whose egress policy permits api.supabase.com and the project's database host.

In that environment: record the ref, read the project to prove it holds no real participant records and is not wired to Production, then apply the exact file whose SHA-256 is recorded above and confirm the applied file matches that digest.
whatWasNotDone: The migration was not applied, to the acceptance project or anywhere else.
No participant-privacy secret was configured in any environment.
No synthetic participant, matter, packet, storage object, legal hold, privacy request or processor outcome was created.
No hosted export, matter-deletion or account-deletion acceptance was run.
No processor callback was configured or contacted.
Production was not touched, and no Production credential was read.
standing: The authorization remains open and unspent. Nothing here consumes it, and applying later needs no new authorization — only an environment that can satisfy the preconditions Roger attached to it.
